---
title: "Automate tasks with triggers"
description: "Use PostgreSQL triggers to automatically execute functions when data changes occur in TimescaleDB hypertables"
products: [cloud, self_hosted]
---

import * as C from "@constants";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";
import TestPlan from "@components/TestPlan.astro";

{C.TIMESCALE_DB} supports {C.PG} triggers on a {C.HYPERTABLE} the same way you use them on a regular table. When you create, alter, drop, enable, or disable a trigger on a {C.HYPERTABLE} — including via `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER` with the `ALL`, `USER`, `ALWAYS`, and `REPLICA` variants — {C.TIMESCALE_DB} propagates the change to every {C.CHUNK}.

## Create a trigger

This example creates a new table called `error_conditions` with the same schema
as `conditions`, but that only stores records which are considered errors. An
error, in this case, is when an application sends a `temperature` or `humidity`
reading with a value that is greater than or equal to 1000.

<NumberedList>

<NumberedItem title="Create a function that inserts erroneous data into the `error_conditions` table">

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION record_error()
  RETURNS trigger AS $record_error$
BEGIN
 IF NEW.temperature >= 1000 OR NEW.humidity >= 1000 THEN
   INSERT INTO error_conditions
     VALUES(NEW.time, NEW.location, NEW.temperature, NEW.humidity);
 END IF;
 RETURN NEW;
END;
$record_error$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create a trigger that calls this function whenever a new row is inserted into the hypertable">

```sql
CREATE TRIGGER record_error
  BEFORE INSERT ON conditions
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION record_error();
```

</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Verify that error rows are captured">

All data is inserted into the `conditions` table, but rows that contain errors
are also added to the `error_conditions` table.

</NumberedItem>

</NumberedList>

For all supported trigger types and clauses, see the [{C.PG} `CREATE TRIGGER` docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createtrigger.html).

## Limitations

- Triggers are not supported on {C.CAGG}s.
- `ROW`-level triggers with transition tables are not supported on {C.HYPERTABLE}s.
- `DELETE` triggers with transition tables are not supported.

<TestPlan>
target: cloud, self-hosted

1. fork the service
2. [cloud] select the service
3. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;`
4. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE conditions (time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, location TEXT, temperature DOUBLE PRECISION, humidity DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.partition_column = 'time');`
5. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE error_conditions (LIKE conditions);`
6. run SQL:
    CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION record_error()
      RETURNS trigger AS $record_error$
    BEGIN
     IF NEW.temperature >= 1000 OR NEW.humidity >= 1000 THEN
       INSERT INTO error_conditions
         VALUES(NEW.time, NEW.location, NEW.temperature, NEW.humidity);
     END IF;
     RETURN NEW;
    END;
    $record_error$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
7. run SQL:
    CREATE TRIGGER record_error
      BEFORE INSERT ON conditions
      FOR EACH ROW
      EXECUTE FUNCTION record_error();
8. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgname = 'record_error' AND tgrelid = 'conditions'::regclass`
9. run SQL: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES (now(), 'office', 70.0, 50.0), (now(), 'lab', 1000.0, 50.0), (now(), 'lab', 70.0, 1000.0);`
10. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM conditions HAVING count(*) = 3`
11. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM error_conditions WHERE temperature >= 1000 OR humidity >= 1000 HAVING count(*) = 2`
12. expect no rows: `SELECT 1 FROM error_conditions WHERE temperature < 1000 AND humidity < 1000`
13. run SQL: `ALTER TABLE conditions DISABLE TRIGGER record_error;`
14. run SQL: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES (now(), 'lab', 1001.0, 50.0);`
15. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM error_conditions HAVING count(*) = 2`
16. run SQL: `ALTER TABLE conditions ENABLE TRIGGER record_error;`
17. run SQL: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES (now(), 'lab', 1002.0, 50.0);`
18. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM error_conditions HAVING count(*) = 3`
19. run SQL: `CREATE FUNCTION ignore_rows() RETURNS trigger AS 'BEGIN RETURN NULL; END;' LANGUAGE plpgsql;`
20. expect error containing `transition tables are not supported on hypertables`: `CREATE TRIGGER audit_rows AFTER INSERT ON conditions REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS new_rows FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ignore_rows()`
21. expect error containing `DELETE triggers with transition tables`: `CREATE TRIGGER audit_deletes AFTER DELETE ON conditions REFERENCING OLD TABLE AS old_rows FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION ignore_rows()`
22. run SQL: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW conditions_hourly WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', time) AS bucket, location, avg(temperature) AS avg_temperature FROM conditions GROUP BY bucket, location WITH NO DATA;`
23. expect error containing `triggers are not supported on continuous aggregate`: `CREATE TRIGGER cagg_trigger INSTEAD OF INSERT ON conditions_hourly FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ignore_rows()`
</TestPlan>
